technique.note: Check body coverage, contrast administration, timing, reconstructions and any limitations against the acquisition. The template supplies example protocol wording.

guidance.title: ACR practice parameter for thoracic CT
ACR practice parameter for abdominal and pelvic CT

lungs-and-airways.note: Localise a pulmonary finding by lobe and record its measured size where applicable. Inspect the airway lumen and walls on the patient series.

pleura-and-pericardium.note: Distinguish pleural and pericardial fluid. Record side, extent and surface abnormalities where visible.

thoracic-lymph-nodes.note: Localise each relevant node to its actual region or station and record its short-axis dimension on the measured image.

comparison.title: Mediastinal nodal annotations on chest CT 0571

heart-and-great-vessels.note: Assess the visible heart, vessels and contrast opacification. A gross organ outline cannot establish luminal patency or exclude embolus.

liver.note: Localise focal findings by lobe or segment. Use the acquired phases to describe attenuation and enhancement and the actual images for lesion size.

comparison.title: Eight liver segments on a separate source MRI

gallbladder-pancreas-and-spleen.note: Assess organ parenchyma, ducts and gallbladder contents on the available phases. Body masks do not trace the duct lumina.

comparison.title: Biliary ducts in the BodyParts3D anatomical atlas

adrenal-glands.note: Record the side of a finding and measure the lesion on the patient images.

kidneys-and-bladder.note: Identify the affected side, inspect the collecting systems and assess the bladder wall with its degree of distension.

bowel-and-peritoneum.note: Name the involved bowel segment and distinguish bowel wall, calibre, peritoneal surface, omental and fluid findings.

reproductive-organs.note: Assess the organs actually present and visible. The source records a female participant but supplies no uterus or adnexal mask.

abdominal-and-pelvic-lymph-nodes.note: Localise individual nodes, distinguish their nodal regions, and record actual short-axis measurements when indicated.

comparison.title: Pelvic nodes on the baseline CT of case 023

bones.note: Inspect all acquired osseous structures in bone windows. Record the site, character and any associated fracture. Count levels against the patient’s anatomy and document variant or partial coverage.

target-lesions.note: Identify the same lesions over time. Use the short axis for nodal targets and longest diameter for non-nodal targets. Assess target, non-target and new disease against the applicable baseline and nadir.

guidance.title: RECIST Working Group, version 1.1
guidance.scope: Target selection, measurement and longitudinal response in applicable solid-tumour studies.

comparison.title: Published target measurements across three scans in case 023
